text:
ashwin: Heads-up — today I saw a cluster of requests where the edge kept streaming to an upstream that was flapping and we ended up with long-lived half-open streams + lots of 499s. thinking we should consider a short-circuit fallback that returns a deterministic partial result after a small window instead of keeping the stream.
maria: Can you paste an example trace? which metric spiked — queue depth or backend latency? :eyes:
ashwin: trace: https://s.re/redwood/trace/abc123 — backend latency shot to 4s+ for ~30s, ingress queue depth doubled, client timeouts followed. many calls were chat-streaming.
ashwin: idea: if upstream doesn't ACK first tokens within 300ms, edge returns a short-circuit frame: linear partial tokens + header X-Edge-Shortcircuit:1 and marks as soft-fallback. clients get partial but app stays responsive.
kai: Tradeoffs: short-circuiting changes semantics for streaming APIs (clients expecting incremental tokens). Might break streaming UX for real-time apps. We need a flag on routes.
maria: Also need to consider billing and metrics — are we charging for tokens generated upstream? If we short-circuit, we should charge only until cutoff and label the billing reason.
zach: Observability-first: we need deterministic signals to trigger. Proposal: composite score = max(upstream_p50_latency, queue_depth_ratio) and a leaky bucket cooldown per tenant. Only trigger if score > threshold for N requests in M seconds.
alexa: ops-bot posted: "alert: ingress.queue_depth > 2x baseline for 30s in us-west-2" — linking to the incident.
ashwin: Example header enforcement (pseudo):
```
# on edge
if not upstream_started and time_since_request_start > 300ms:
  return shortcircuit_response(partial_payload, headers={"X-Edge-Shortcircuit":"1"})
```
maria: We should define the partial_payload semantics. Maybe synthesize placeholder tokens like "[partial output due to upstream overload]" vs returning what we already buffered from upstream. Placeholder safer for correctness.
kai: For idempotency & side effects: only allow short-circuit for read-only inference endpoints. No short-circuit for endpoints with verified side effects (calls to billing, db writes, webhook triggers).
zach: Observability plumbing: add metrics: edge.shortcircuit.count, edge.shortcircuit.reason (latency|queue|upstream-error), edge.shortcircuit.duration; and trace span tag edge.shortcircuit=true.
ashwin: Experiment plan: A/B on non-critical routes (internal bots / examples) for 2 weeks. 1% baseline, ramp to 10% if errors down and SLOs improve. Track user-visible errors, median latency, 499 rate, and model-quality regressions from eval set.
alexa: ops-bot: scheduled runbook snippet: "If shortcircuit rate > 5% tenant-wide for > 10m, rollback the policy and alert infra@".
maria: We'll also need client SDK changes: expose header and a helper flag on stream to indicate a partial response was delivered. Back compat: default behaviour unchanged unless route opts-in.
kai: One more: fallback persistence — we might want to cache partial results for quick recovery on retry. But caching streams has complexity (incomplete context). start simple: no cache.
zach: Agreed. I'll draft a telemetry RFC with scoring formula and metric names, plus a simple state machine for cooldown and per-tenant rate limits.
ashwin: thanks — I'll stub the canary config and add a note to the rollout checklist: "ensure route flag + SDK opt-in + billing label mapping".
alexa: ops-bot: reminder set for 2 weeks -> follow-up review meeting. :white_check_mark:
maria: Love it. low-risk experiment if we guard it tightly.
kai: ok — assign owners? zach on telemetry, ashwin on edge impl, maria on billing & SDK, i'll review the code changes.
ashwin: assigned. starting PR today.
